thread:
kyle_support: FYI - AtlasHealth escalated, embeddings endpoint returning dimension mismatch intermittently when using our TS SDK batcher. Ticket INC-23456.
alex_g: their error: `400 Bad Request - embedding vector size mismatch: expected 1536, got 1535` — happens only on large bulk uploads (500+ texts) with client concurrency and retries enabled.
customer-atlas: repro steps we ran: send 500 texts with ts-sdk v1.3.7, batch size 16, concurrency 8, backoff retries default. After ~200 items we see sporadic 400s. When we retry the same request individually it succeeds.
support-bot: Logged request ids: r-01GXZ9A4, r-01GXZ9B1, r-01GXZ9B9. Customer provided sample payload & stacktrace.
alex_g: attaching minimal repro (ts):
```
await embedClient.createEmbeddings({
  model: 'open-embed-2-small',
  input: bulkTexts,
  batchSize: 16,
  concurrency: 8,
  retry: {retries: 3}
});
```
alex_g: customer says if they set concurrency=1 or batchSize=1 errors stop. Also Python SDK v0.9.5 and Go v0.8.2 are fine for them (no errors) but when they port to TS we see the issue.
devon: interesting — runtime accepts a batch payload and validates vector length server-side. If a single vector is truncated client-side it will return 400. Could be byte-length miscalc during serialization.
sre-jen: I pulled logs for r-01GXZ9A4: on the server we see a JSON body with an embeddings array length 1536 for most items, but one item has length 1535. The HTTP body size for that request is slightly smaller than expected. Tracing headers show requests originated from ts-sdk host ip 34.12.87.9. Attaching excerpt.
maria: billing note — customer saw a 3x token+request spike due to retries, want credits if we confirm bug.
alex_g: can you paste the failing item input text? customer provided this small string: "Patient notes: follow-up in 3 months" — short, shouldn't cause anything weird.
tom: model open-embed-2-small dim confirmed at 1536 on our catalog.
devon: quick hypothesis: TS SDK batcher merges multiple in-flight arrays into a single Float32Array buffer and we might have an off-by-one when concatenating last vector if a retry cancels mid-serialization. That would yield one vector shorter by 1.
alex_g: customer also shared TS stacktrace: `TypeError: buffer.copy is copying 1535 floats when original is 1536` — looks like a client bug.
kyle_support: immediate mitigation we told customer: downgrade to Python/Go SDKs or set concurrency=1 / batchSize<=4 and set retry.retries=0 until patch. They asked for a timeline.
devon: eng-runtime: we should make server validation return a clear error code and include index of offending vector (we currently return generic 400). Also will add a sanity check comparing summed byte-length vs expected and log input checksum to help repro.
sre-jen: I've opened a trace link and enabled verbose body logging for the next hour for their IP.
alex_g: can eng-oss/devex triage TS SDK v1.3.7? If patch quick we can ask AtlasHealth to test.
devon: creating PR to TS SDK: fix buffer concatenation edge-case when last chunk length % bytesPerVector != 0. Will release v1.3.8-rc1 tonight. Patch also exposes a DEBUG env var to dump preflight vector lengths.
maria: PM asks for impact: which customers could hit this? Looks like any user using TS SDK + batching + concurrency with models whose vector size > 512. We should notify churn risk and offering temporary credits.
kyle_support: noted. I've updated INC-23456 with mitigation steps and requested test from customer once we have rc. Also asked for billing hold until we confirm.
customer-atlas: appreciate fast response. We can test rc tomorrow morning.
alex_g: next steps: (1) devon pushes RC, (2) support runs repro with rc (3) eng-runtime adds clearer error index and request checksum logging, (4) decide on credits after root cause. Anyone object?
all: nope.
kyle_support: I'll close loop with customer and ping here when they finish test. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
